# Improving autogenerated migrations

A generated migration is the template diff between two renders. Real
pipelines have customised the text around it, so many hunks conflict, or
get applied where maintainers chose not to. The merged template sync PRs
of the nf-core pipelines are the ground truth: replay them, see where
nf-migrate disagrees with the maintainers, and change the migration (or an
operation, when the pattern recurs) until what is left are decisions only a
maintainer can make.

All tooling is in `scripts/learn/`. Run everything from the repo root.

## Ground rules

- **The render invariant is non-negotiable.** Applied to its
  `down_revision`'s render, each migration must give its own render byte
  for byte, and on its own render every operation must be already applied.
  Run `check_renders.py` after every change. A fix that breaks it is wrong,
  however much it raises the score.
- **Conceptually the same, not byte-identical.** A sync PR also carries
  fixes, module updates and CHANGELOG entries. Scores only count the lines
  a template change adds or removes, whitespace-insensitive. Do not chase
  one pipeline's idiosyncrasy: act on patterns seen in at least 3–4 PRs.
- **Learn from single-release PRs.** In a PR spanning several releases, an
  early conflict leaves a file in its old state and every later change to
  it fails too. `worklist.py` already filters to single-step PRs.
- **Never hand-edit a migration file directly.** `nf-migrate revision`
  regenerates it and the edit is lost. Hand edits are scripts in
  `scripts/learn/edits/vX_Y_Z.py`, re-applied by `rebuild.sh`.
- **A recurring pattern belongs in the generator or an operation,** not in
  forty hand edits. Fix it in `autogenerate.py` / `operations.py` /
  `yaml_edit.py` test-first, regenerate, and measure the whole chain.
- **Measure every change both ways.** Keep the previous `eval.jsonl` and
  run `compare.py`: a change is kept only if "better" clearly outnumbers
  "worse", and the worse cases are single-pipeline judgment calls.

## Setup (once)

Needs about 6 GB for clones. Full clones, not blob-less: the evaluator
reads blobs from many commits.

```bash
# Every nf-core pipeline (names from https://nf-co.re/pipelines.json).
mkdir -p data/pipelines
while read -r name; do
  git clone --quiet --no-single-branch \
    "https://github.com/nf-core/$name.git" "data/pipelines/$name"
done < names.txt

# Renders of every release in the chain, tagged vX.Y.Z (see README "Adding
# a migration"): pass every version from 1.9 to the newest, in order.
scripts/build_template_history.sh scripts/sentinel.nf-core.yml data/history \
  1.9 $(grep -h "^revision" src/nf_migrate/nf_core_migrations/*.py \
    | cut -d"'" -f2 | sort -V)

# nf-core/tools CHANGELOG, for migration docstrings.
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/tools/main/CHANGELOG.md \
  > data/CHANGELOG.md

# Merged template updates: one JSON line per sync PR merge.
uv run python scripts/learn/collect.py data/pipelines > data/merges.jsonl
```

Keep `data/` out of git.

## The loop

```bash
export NF_MIGRATE_PIPELINES=data/pipelines
M=src/nf_migrate/nf_core_migrations

# 1. Evaluate the whole chain on every PR; score per release.
uv run python scripts/learn/evaluate.py data/merges.jsonl data/history $M data/eval.jsonl
uv run python scripts/learn/scores.py data/eval.jsonl $M        # release  PRs  agree/total  score

# 2. Pick a release (in order on a first pass, lowest score after) and
#    list what is learnable: conflicts the maintainers applied.
uv run python scripts/learn/worklist.py data/eval.jsonl --rev 3.4.0 --min 4
uv run python scripts/learn/report.py summary data/eval.jsonl --rev 3.4.0 --top 15

# 3. Look at the samples: how pipelines' text differed from the template's
#    old text, and what the maintainers merged.
uv run python scripts/learn/triage.py data/eval.jsonl data/merges.jsonl $M 3.4.0 \
  --only 50 61 63 --samples 3 --width 120

# 4. Edit (see below), then rebuild and check the invariant.
cp data/eval.jsonl data/eval-before.jsonl
scripts/learn/rebuild.sh data/history data/CHANGELOG.md     # ends with check_renders

# 5. Measure.
uv run python scripts/learn/evaluate.py data/merges.jsonl data/history $M data/eval.jsonl
uv run python scripts/learn/compare.py data/eval-before.jsonl data/eval.jsonl 3.4.0
```

`evaluate.py --covers 3.4.0` limits a run to PRs whose range includes a
release, for a quick iteration. Record each release's before → after score
and what you changed; on the second pass start from the lowest scores.

### Reading triage output

Each sample shows `OUTCOME message human=<exact>/<conceptual>`:

- `CONFLICT … human=applied` — **learnable**: the maintainers made the
  change, nf-migrate could not place it. The "before vs template old" diff
  shows what the pipeline had instead.
- `APPLIED … human=kept` — over-applied: maintainers declined it (often
  template boilerplate in README/docs). Fix only if the pattern is clear.
- `ALREADY_APPLIED … human=partial` — a false "already applied", usually a
  deletion whose context line still exists.
- `before: nothing similar` — the pipeline rewrote the region, or an
  earlier release in the same PR conflicted (cascade); usually not
  learnable.

## Choosing a fix

Match the variation you see to the narrowest tool:

| What pipelines did | Fix |
|---|---|
| Re-aligned, trimmed, re-indented, `**`/`__`, `*`/`-` bullets, deleted `TODO nf-core` notes | Already tolerated by `Replace`; if not, it is a generator/operation bug |
| Kept some sections of a large template deletion | `RemoveText` per paragraph (generator does this for pure deletions) |
| Customised a value or line inside the hunk | `varying(op, ["line text"])` → `RegexReplace` keeping that line |
| Extended the neighbouring block the hunk is anchored on | `RegexReplace` anchored on a stable line elsewhere (the next block, the file end) |
| Passes extra arguments to a call / extra `take:` inputs | Append after the call's last argument (see `edits/v3_4_0.py`) |
| Same change wanted in every occurrence | `every=True` (`Replace` or `RegexReplace`) |
| Version on a line they also edited | `BumpVersion` (generator emits it for one-line bumps) |
| YAML value, key or CI step | `YamlSet` / `YamlListItem` (generator emits them when the YAML diff reproduces the hunk) |
| Release rewrote the file and maintainers took the template's | `ReplaceFile` with an `already` marker of the new structure, plus a `ManualStep` to port their code |
| Pipeline-owned code or prose rewritten case by case | Leave it as a conflict |

Always wrap a tolerant variant as `FirstOf(<exact generated op>, <tolerant
op>)`, so untouched pipelines (and the renders) get the template's text
exactly.

## Writing an edit script

`scripts/learn/edits/vX_Y_Z.py`, run with `scripts/learn` on `PYTHONPATH`
and `NF_MIGRATE_HISTORY` set by `rebuild.sh`:

```python
from editops import find, first_of, load, migration_path, original_source, regex, replace_ops

path = migration_path("3.1.0")
operations = load(path).operations
mono = find(operations, "nextflow.config",
            new_contains="    monochromeLogs = params.monochrome_logs\n")
replace_ops(path, {
    mono: first_of("nextflow.config", [
        original_source(path, mono),
        regex(
            "nextflow.config",
            r"^([ \t]*)defaultIgnoreParams\s*=.*\n",
            r"\g<0>\1monochromeLogs = params.monochrome_logs\n",
            r"\A(?=[\s\S]*^[ \t]*monochromeLogs\s*=)[\s\S]*",
            "",
        ),
    ], "Hand-edited: pipelines ignore their own parameters in\n"
       "defaultIgnoreParams, which this was anchored on."),
})
```

- **Find operations by content, never by index**: `find(ops, path,
  old_equals=…, new_contains=…, text_startswith=…, kind="RemoveText")`.
  Indices shift on every regeneration. `find` looks inside a generated
  `FirstOf` at its first operation.
- **Every hand-edited operation gets a `Hand-edited:` comment** saying
  which pipeline variation it tolerates and why.
- **`applied` must cover the match**, or a second run applies again.
  For an insertion before an anchor, cover anchor and insert
  (`r"^[ \t]*arm \{[\s\S]*?^    singularity \{\n"`), or use the whole-file
  idiom `r"\A(?=[\s\S]*MARKER)[\s\S]*"`: already applied whenever the
  marker is anywhere, which also avoids duplicating a block a pipeline
  already has elsewhere.
- **Replacements are templates**: double backslashes in literal text
  (`text.replace("\\", "\\\\")`); use `\g<0>` / named groups.
  `{{placeholders}}` work in patterns and are matched literally.
- Use `original_source(path, index)` for the exact generated op inside
  `first_of`, not a rebuilt one: rebuilding drops fields like `every`.
- Do not re-indent nested sources: it changes template text inside
  triple-quoted strings (`first_of` already leaves them as they are).

## Changing operations or the generator

- Test first: Given / When / Then tests in `tests/test_operations.py`,
  `tests/test_yaml_set.py` or `tests/test_autogenerate.py`, watch them fail,
  then implement.
- A new operation must be imported by generated modules (`_render_module`
  in `autogenerate.py`) and scored by `scripts/learn/evaluate.py`
  (`human_status`, `scored_kinds`), or its agreement is invisible.
- After generator changes, `rebuild.sh`, then the whole-chain evaluation
  and `compare.py`. Expect some releases to move both ways; keep the
  change only if the net is clearly positive.
- Finish with `uv run pytest -n auto`, `uv run ruff check .`,
  `uv run ruff format --check .` and the end-to-end check: upgrading the
  1.9 render (without `.nf-core.yml`) to 3.3.1 and 4.1.0 with the CLI must
  leave every text file identical to those renders.

## Known traps

- Merges committed with conflict markers hold both sides; the evaluator
  skips those files, do not learn from them by hand either.
- Some TEMPLATE renders carry nf-core/tools bugs (3.3.x
  `runs-on=$-nf-test`). The render is the truth for the invariant; the
  maintainers' hand fix is not something to encode.
- A text heuristic that tests "is it already done" against line counts is
  fragile: generic lines (`"type": "string",`, `}`) recur across a file.
  Check the render invariant before trusting it.
- Report the outcome with numbers: per-release before → after, and
  `docs/validation.md` updated when the chain's figures change.
